blocks.text: Sine ka inverse ban gaya. Ab bari cosine ki hai. Tareeqa bilkul wahi hai, lekin ek farq dhyan se dekhiyega: cosine ke liye restricted interval sine wala nahin hoga. Yahi farq is sabaq ki jaan hai, aur imtihan mein sab se zyada ghaltiyan isi jagah hoti hain. Sabaq ke aakhir mein hum sine aur cosine ke inverse ka ek muqabla (comparison) table bhi banayenge, taa ke dono ka farq hamesha ke liye zehan mein baith jaye.

Kitab kehti hai: function \(f : \mathbb{R} \to [-1, 1]\) ko dekhiye jo \(f(x) = \cos x\) se defined hai. Is ka graph Figure 9.4 mein hai. Domain poora \(\mathbb{R}\), aur codomain \([-1, 1]\), kyun ke cosine ki value bhi hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan rehti hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Yahan bhi kitab mein "define by" chhapa hai; sahi "defined by" hai. Sirf grammar ki ghalti hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = cos x from minus 4 pi to 4 pi. The wave has maximum value 1 at even multiples of pi and minimum value minus 1 at odd multiples of pi; dashed lines y = 1 and y = minus 1 touch it at all these points.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.4: Graph of f(x) = cos x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Kitab aage kehti hai: sine ki tarah cosine ka graph bhi bijective nahin, kyun ke yeh bhi horizontal line test mein fail ho jata hai. Yeh line \(y = 1\) aur \(y = -1\) ko kai jagah chhoota hai. Lekin agar hum soch samajh kar \(f(x) = \cos x\) ke domain ko closed interval \([0, \pi]\) tak restrict kar dein, to restricted function \(f : [0, \pi] \to [-1, 1]\) one-one aur onto ban jata hai, yani invertible, aur ise principal cosine function kehte hain. Inverse cosine function yun defined hai:

blocks.text_alt: y equals cosine inverse of x if and only if x equals cosine of y

blocks.text: \(\cos^{-1} x\) ka domain \([-1, 1]\) hai aur range \([0, \pi]\) hai. Yani input koi bhi number \(-1\) se \(1\) tak ho sakta hai, aur jawab hamesha \(0\) se \(\pi\) tak ka koi angle hoga.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se aham sawal: sine wala interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) yahan kyun nahin chalta? Kyun ke wahan cosine one-to-one nahin hai. Dekhiye: \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\). Cosine even function hai, yani \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\), is liye negative angle aur us ka positive jora hamesha ek hi value dete hain. Upar se, us interval par cosine kabhi negative hota hi nahin, to woh \([-1, 1]\) par onto bhi nahin hoga.
\([0, \pi]\) par Figure 9.4 dekhiye: cosine \(1\) se (angle \(0\) par) lagataar gir kar \(-1\) tak (angle \(\pi\) par) aata hai. Yani \([-1, 1]\) ki har value sirf ek baar leta hai: one-to-one bhi aur onto bhi.
Do ranges saath saath yaad kijiye: \(\sin^{-1}\) ke jawab \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein (pehla aur chautha quadrant); \(\cos^{-1}\) ke jawab \([0, \pi]\) mein (pehla aur doosra quadrant). Ek aasan jumla: "sine daayen taraf, cosine upar ki taraf", kyun ke unit circle par \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) daayen aadhe hisse ko aur \([0, \pi]\) upar wale aadhe hisse ko dhakta hai.

blocks.caption: Domain aur range ki adla badli (hamara khulasa)

blocks.text: Kitab ke mutabiq function \(\cos : [0, \pi] \to [-1, 1]\) ka graph Figure 9.5(a) mein hai, aur \(\cos^{-1} : [-1, 1] \to [0, \pi]\) ka graph Figure 9.5(b) mein hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = cos x only from 0 to pi. It falls steadily from the point (0, 1), crosses the x-axis at pi over 2, and ends at the point (pi, minus 1).
blocks.caption: Figure 9.5(a): Graph of y = cos x from 0 to π (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.alt: Graph of y = inverse cosine of x from minus 1 to 1. It falls from the point (minus 1, pi), crosses the y-axis at pi over 2, and ends at the point (1, 0).
blocks.caption: Figure 9.5(b): Graph of y = cos⁻¹ x from −1 to 1 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Points phir jagah badalte hain: cosine graph ke \((0, 1)\) aur \((\pi, -1)\) inverse cosine graph par \((1, 0)\) aur \((-1, \pi)\) ban jate hain. Figure 9.5(a) ka \(x\)-intercept \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)\) Figure 9.5(b) ka \(y\)-intercept \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) ban gaya, kyun ke \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) ka matlab hai \(\cos^{-1} 0 = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
Figure 9.5(b) ka curve baayen se daayen neeche aa raha hai: \(\cos^{-1} x\) ek decreasing (ghatne wala) function hai. Bara number, chhota angle. Yeh sine ke ulat hai, jahan \(\sin^{-1} x\) barhne wala function tha.

blocks.caption: Principal inverse cosine ki kuch values (hamari table; har value [0, π] mein hai)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table mein negative inputs ko ghor se dekhiye: yeh obtuse angles (\(90^\circ\) se bare) dete hain. Maslan \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai, \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) nahin, kyun ke negative angles range \([0, \pi]\) se bahar hain. Doosre quadrant mein cosine negative hota hai, is liye negative value ka angle wahin milta hai.
Table se ek pattern nazar aata hai: \(\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cos^{-1} x\). Maslan \(\frac{2\pi}{3} = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3}\), aur \(\frac{5\pi}{6} = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6}\). Yeh is liye sahi hai ke \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\). (Sine ke liye pattern alag hai: \(\sin^{-1}(-x) = -\sin^{-1} x\). Dono ko gadmad na kijiye.)
Khud sochiye: \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\) kya hoga? (Pehle \(\cos^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}\); phir pattern se \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{4}\). Yeh \([0, \pi]\) mein hai, to jawab \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\).)

Kitab batati hai ke \(\cos^{-1} x\) ka graph principal cosine function \(y = \cos x\) ke graph ko line \(y = x\) mein aaine ki tarah ulta kar ke bhi milta hai, jaisa Figure 9.6 mein hai. Yahan bhi \(y = \cos x\) aur \(y = \cos^{-1} x\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se ek doosre ka aaina hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "is also obtain by reflecting" chhapa hai; sahi "is also obtained by reflecting" hai. Aur kitab likhti hai "Observe that the graph of \(y = \cos x\) is symmetric about the line \(y = x\)". Akela \(y = \cos x\) ka graph \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se symmetric nahin. Sahi baat: \(y = \cos x\) (principal) aur \(y = \cos^{-1} x\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) ke lihaaz se symmetric hain, yani ek doosre ke aaine hain.

blocks.alt: The principal cosine curve from (0, 1) to (pi, minus 1) and the inverse cosine curve from (minus 1, pi) to (1, 0), drawn together with the dashed line y = x. Each curve is the mirror image of the other in that line.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.6: y = cos x and y = cos⁻¹ x are mirror images in the line y = x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Figure 9.6 mein dono curves ek doosre ko line \(y = x\) par kaat te hain, us point par jahan \(\cos x = x\) hota hai (taqreeban \(x \approx 0.739\)). Function aur us ka inverse sirf aaine wali line par, ya aaine ke joron mein, milte hain; kahin aur achanak nahin.
Ghar par try kijiye: Figure 9.5(a) ko graph paper par banaiye aur kaghaz ko line \(y = x\) par mor kar dekhiye ke curve Figure 9.5(b) jaisa banta hai ya nahin.

Kitab aage kehti hai: sine ki tarah, range \([-1, 1]\) wale cosine function ko bhi laatadaad intervals mein se kisi ek par restrict kar sakte hain, jaise \([-2\pi, -\pi]\), \([-\pi, 0]\), \([0, \pi]\), \([\pi, 2\pi]\), ya aam shakal mein \([n\pi, n\pi + \pi]\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\); is se cosine one-to-one ban jata hai. Agar koi interval na bataya jaye, to \(\cos^{-1} x\) woh function hai jis ka domain \([-1, 1]\) aur range \([0, \pi]\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Har interval ki lambai \(\pi\) hai, aur har ek cosine ki ek choti (maximum ya minimum) se agli choti tak jata hai (Figure 9.4 ke dots dekhiye). Is liye har interval par cosine ya to lagataar ghatta hai ya lagataar barhta hai. Standard intikhab \(n = 0\), yani \([0, \pi]\), hai, aur is ki values principal values kehlati hain. Sine ke intervals \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke odd multiples se shuru hote the, cosine ke intervals \(\pi\) ke multiples se shuru hote hain: yeh farq bhi yaad rakhiye. Khud sochiye: interval \([\pi, 2\pi]\) par cosine barhta hai ya ghatta hai? (Barhta hai: \(\cos\pi = -1\) se \(\cos 2\pi = 1\) tak. Is liye wahan bhi one-to-one hai, magar standard intikhab phir bhi \([0, \pi]\) hi rehta hai.)

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: \(\cos^{-1} x \ne (\cos x)^{-1}\) ya \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\) to \(\sec x\) hai. Hamari misaal: \(\cos^{-1} 0 = \frac{\pi}{2}\), jab ke \(\frac{1}{\cos 0} = 1\). Bilkul alag jawab! \(\cos^{-1}\) mein \(-1\) inverse function ka naam hai, power nahin. Is farq ka ek aur saboot domain hai: \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\) ke liye \(x\) koi bhi angle ho sakta hai (siwaye un ke jahan \(\cos x = 0\)), jab ke \(\cos^{-1} x\) ke liye \(x\) sirf \(-1\) se \(1\) tak ka number ho sakta hai. Jin do cheezon ke domain hi alag hon, woh ek function kaise ho sakti hain?

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Teen chhoti misaalein, har ek do qadam mein (pehle iff, phir range check):
(a) \(\cos^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\): \(\cos y = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), aur \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) range \([0, \pi]\) mein hai. Jawab \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).
(b) \(\cos^{-1}(-1)\): \(\cos y = -1\), aur \(\pi\) range mein hai (\(-\pi\) ya \(3\pi\) nahin). Jawab \(\pi\).
(c) \(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\): \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hai, is liye jawab \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) nahin. \(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}\), aur \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\). Jawab \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\).

blocks.caption: Inverse sine aur inverse cosine ka muqabla (hamari table)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is table ko imtihan se pehle ek baar zaroor dohraiye. Dono functions ka domain bilkul ek jaisa hai, is liye students samajhte hain ke range bhi ek jaisi hogi; yahi sab se bari ghalat fehmi hai. Farq sirf range ka hai, lekin isi farq se jawab badal jata hai.
Ek aasan misaal se sochiye: ek dukaan ke do counters hain. Sine wala counter sirf "daayen taraf" ke angles deta hai (\(-90^\circ\) se \(90^\circ\)), cosine wala counter sirf "upar" ke angles deta hai (\(0^\circ\) se \(180^\circ\)). Aap kisi bhi counter par koi bhi number \(-1\) se \(1\) tak de sakte hain, lekin har counter apne hi hisse ka angle wapas karega.
Khud sochiye: kya koi aisa \(x\) hai jis ke liye \(\sin^{-1} x\) aur \(\cos^{-1} x\) barabar hon? (Haan, \(x = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) par dono \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hain. 9.1.6 ki Example 5 mein aap dekhenge ke hamesha \(\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) hota hai; \(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\) is ki tasdeeq karta hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Principal cosine function: \(\cos : [0, \pi] \to [-1, 1]\), jo bijective hai.
2. \(y = \cos^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \cos y\); domain \([-1, 1]\), range \([0, \pi]\).
3. Negative number ka \(\cos^{-1}\) obtuse angle hota hai, \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\) mein; kabhi negative angle nahin.
4. \(y = \cos^{-1} x\) ka graph principal cosine ke graph ka \(y = x\) mein aaina hai; yeh \((-1, \pi)\) se \((1, 0)\) tak neeche aata hai.
5. \(\cos^{-1} x\) ka matlab \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\) nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Cosine ke liye sine wali range lagana: \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{3}\) ghalat hai; jawab \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.
2. \(\cos^{-1} 1 = 2\pi\) likhna: \(2\pi\) range \([0, \pi]\) se bahar hai; jawab \(0\) hai.
3. \(\sin^{-1}(-x) = -\sin^{-1} x\) wala rule cosine par lagana: cosine ke liye rule \(\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cos^{-1} x\) hai.
4. \(\cos^{-1} x\) ko \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\) samajhna.
